parts.text:
1
A student estimates the maximum speed of some different moving objects.
Which maximum speed is not a reasonable estimate?
A
container ship: 10 m s–1
B
Olympic sprinter: 0.1 km s–1
C
racing car: 9000 cm s–1
D
snail: 0.01 km h–1

hints: Convert all four speeds to the same unit, $\text{m s}^{-1}$, because the question mixes $\text{m s}^{-1}$, $\text{km s}^{-1}$, $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ and $\text{km h}^{-1}$.
Recall that an Olympic $100 \text{m}$ sprint takes about $10 \text{s}$, so a human maximum is near $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ for comparison.
Multiply out $0.1 \text{km s}^{-1}$ using $1 \text{km} = 1000 \text{m}$ and $9000 \text{cm s}^{-1}$ using $100 \text{cm} = 1 \text{m}$, then check which converted value is far from real life.
walkthrough: Put every estimate in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ to compare fairly, using $1 \text{km} = 1000 \text{m}$, $1 \text{m} = 100 \text{cm}$ and $1 \text{h} = 3600 \text{s}$.
Container ship: already $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which matches a fast ship of order tens of knots and is reasonable.

Olympic sprinter: $0.1 \text{km s}^{-1} = 0.1 \times 1000 \text{m s}^{-1} = 100 \text{m s}^{-1}$. A $100 \text{m}$ race in about $10 \text{s}$ gives $v \approx 100/10 = 10 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so $100 \text{m s}^{-1}$ is about 10 times too large.
Racing car: $9000 \text{cm s}^{-1} = 9000/100 \text{m s}^{-1} = 90 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which is a Formula 1 type speed and is reasonable.
Snail: $0.01 \text{km h}^{-1} = 10 \text{m h}^{-1} = 10/3600 \text{m s}^{-1} \approx 0.003 \text{m s}^{-1}$, a slow crawl and is reasonable.
Only the sprinter value is unreasonably high. This is option B.

A.explanation: About $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ is about $36 \text{km h}^{-1}$, a reasonable maximum for a large container ship.

B.explanation: $0.1 \text{km s}^{-1} = 100 \text{m s}^{-1}$, about ten times faster than a $100 \text{m}$ sprint in $10 \text{s}$, so it is not reasonable.

C.explanation: $9000 \text{cm s}^{-1} = 90 \text{m s}^{-1}$, about $324 \text{km h}^{-1}$, a reasonable maximum for a racing car.

D.explanation: $0.01 \text{km h}^{-1} = 10 \text{m h}^{-1}$, about $0.003 \text{m s}^{-1}$, a reasonable crawling speed for a snail.
